menu.tooltiptext: Managed Windows identity and proxy authentication

field.description: Enable the managed gateway after selecting the access mode and client interfaces. Kerberos and NTLM modes remain disabled until their Domain and Keytab prerequisites are complete. Transparent without identification requires no domain membership.

Transparent without identification: select the mode, interfaces and inspection level, then enable and save.
Transparent identification: configure the IP policy mappings and optional station enrollment.
Kerberos or NTLM: save the domain values, complete Domain and Keytab, then return here to enable.
The standalone Kontrol-ID engine is activated only when the prerequisites of the selected mode are ready.

Client → Kontrol-ID secure web gateway → Internet
Kontrol-ID is the multithread proxy, authentication endpoint, TLS inspection point and policy engine. No Squid or ICAP chain is used. Explicit clients connect to the HTTP listener configured below; transparent interception is managed directly by the engine.

Transparent identification first resolves the logged-on Windows user, then falls back to the enrolled workstation hostname. Only when neither identity is available is the configured Unknown User Fallback applied; the proxy never sends an authentication challenge in this mode. Transparent without identification skips identity processing and applies the default policy group, while preserving optional IP exceptions and overrides. Explicit mode requires clients to use the proxy address or PAC/WPAD. The standalone engine supports native Kerberos/SPNEGO, NTLMv2, and HTTP Basic backed by the selected Kontrol authentication server.

Kerberos/SPNEGO is recommended and validates browser tickets against the package-owned keytab. The combined mode tries Kerberos first and only falls back to NTLMv2 for legacy domain clients. NTLM challenges are validated through Winbind; NTLMv1 and LM are not accepted. HTTP Basic uses the selected local or LDAP authentication server and should only be used on a trusted client network because proxy credentials are not independently encrypted on the client-to-proxy connection.

option.name: HTTP Basic (Local or LDAP; trusted LAN only)

field.description: DNS name used by explicit proxy clients and by the Kerberos HTTP service principal, for example proxy.example.corp.
DNS domain used for Kerberos/NTLM, for example example.corp. The Kerberos realm is generated in uppercase.
FQDN of the preferred AD controller. DNS and time synchronization must be functional before joining.
Short NetBIOS domain name used by Samba/Winbind, for example EXAMPLE.

Maximum simultaneous gateway workers. Each request is handled independently by the native multithread engine. Start with 256 and size this value from measured concurrency, CPU and memory; supported range is 64 to 20000.

Controls how Kontrol-ID activates generated policy, list and group changes. Reload with USR1 preserves the running process, worker threads and active connections and is recommended for ordinary policy changes. Choose a restart action after changing worker count, listener ports, authentication, TLS inspection or other engine-wide settings. A change between transparent identification, anonymous transparent mode and explicit proxy authentication always triggers one controlled restart, even when USR1 is selected, because the authentication plugin itself must be replaced.

option.name: Reload lists and groups with USR1 (preserve active connections)
Restart using the Kontrol-ID rc.d service
Kill the running engine and start a new copy

field.description: HTTP-only is the safe onboarding mode. HTTP + HTTPS enables native Kontrol-ID TLS inspection with the certificate authority selected below. Every inspected client must trust that CA before HTTPS interception is enabled.

Blocks QUIC on UDP port 443 for transparent HTTPS clients, forcing standards-compliant browsers to retry over inspected HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 on TCP. Keep this enabled while Kontrol-ID does not provide native HTTP/3 inspection. Proxy bypass sources, destinations and private networks remain exempt. This option applies only to transparent HTTP + HTTPS inspection.
Interfaces where Kontrol-ID listens for explicit clients or installs transparent HTTP/HTTPS redirects.

Select the certificate authority used to generate HTTPS inspection certificates and to enroll Windows endpoints. Kontrol-ID Internal CA is the recommended default. A custom corporate CA must contain its private key on this appliance, be currently valid and be authorized to sign certificates. Clients must trust the public certificate of the selected CA.

Client-facing HTTP listener used by explicit proxy clients and transparent HTTP redirection. Changing it automatically updates the managed firewall rules; explicit clients, PAC and GPO settings must be updated separately.
Internal TLS inspection listener. It must differ from the HTTP listener. In transparent mode, Kontrol-ID also updates the corresponding PF redirection automatically.

In transparent modes, pass RFC 1918 destination networks directly instead of sending them through Kontrol-ID. This remains visible in explicit mode for configuration consistency, but explicit clients must use PAC/GPO DIRECT rules to bypass the proxy itself.

Source IPs, CIDR networks or firewall aliases that bypass transparent interception completely. Separate entries with semicolons. In explicit mode, source bypass must be configured as DIRECT in PAC/GPO because the client has already selected the proxy before connecting.

Destination IPs, CIDR networks, hostnames, firewall aliases or full URLs that bypass transparent interception. Separate entries with semicolons. A URL is reduced to its hostname because the path is not available before interception; hostnames are resolved when the rules are applied.

Sites that must remain proxied but must not have HTTPS decrypted, useful for banks, certificate-pinned applications and problematic services. Enter one hostname, IP or URL per line. *.example.com is accepted and normalized to the E2Guardian domain-list format. Full URLs are reduced to their hostname because a URL path is visible only after TLS interception. For path-specific filtering exceptions, use the Site Lists and URL Lists policy pages.
Optional limiter for explicit proxy clients. For transparent clients, apply limiters in the firewall rules on the intercepted interface.
Optional upload limiter for explicit proxy clients. Select a download limiter as well when enabling this option.
Native Windows WinRM HTTPS listener port.
TCP and TLS connection timeout in milliseconds.
Maximum duration of a WinRM identity request in milliseconds.
Require the endpoint certificate to be issued by the selected Kontrol-ID CA.
Require the enrolled hostname to match the endpoint certificate SAN.
Seconds to retain a successful automatic identity.
Seconds before retrying an unknown or unreachable station.
Seconds a previous successful identity may be reused during a temporary endpoint failure.
Lifetime of a manually authenticated IP session in seconds.
Identity recorded by Kontrol-ID when automatic identification is unavailable.

Applied only after both automatic user lookup and enrolled-hostname fallback fail. Redirect blocks navigation until the user authenticates against the selected Kontrol local or directory backend. HTTPS redirection requires HTTP + HTTPS inspection and a trusted Kontrol-ID CA. Deny access uses the selected standard block page.

When the Portal URL is empty, issue a dedicated server certificate for the local portal using the selected Kontrol-ID CA and activate it on the WebGUI. The certificate includes the portal FQDN, short hostname and local interface IPs as Subject Alternative Names. The previous WebGUI certificate is preserved and restored if this option is disabled or the package is removed.
Leave empty to use the Kontrol WebGUI hostname and /kontrol_id_portal.php.
Visual style shown to unidentified users. All templates contain the same authentication fields, validation and administrator message.

Message shown when the user needs an account or administrative assistance. Plain text and the following safe HTML tags are accepted: p, br, strong, b, em, i, u, ul, ol, li, small, code. Attributes, scripts, styles and embedded content are removed. The Custom Message template displays this content prominently.

Basic authentication and the fallback portal reuse a server from System > User Manager > Authentication Servers without duplicating its credentials. Kerberos and NTLM domain membership are managed separately under Domain and Keytab. The local database remains available for networks without Active Directory.
Select the Kontrol local database or an LDAP/AD authentication server already managed by the base system. Credentials are never copied into the Kontrol-ID package configuration.
Local Kontrol users must belong to this non-administrative group.
Comma-separated AD/LDAP group names. Matching is case-insensitive.
Download a versioned XML file containing the Kontrol-ID identity, engine and policy configuration.
Log endpoint query failures to the system log. Passwords and certificates are never logged.
